location_qualifier: beaches and hinterland west of the Matanikau; army assembled on the island by mid-October
composing_text: The 2nd Division and the survivors of the Kawaguchi and Ichiki Forces were then on the island; two battalions of the 38th Division were also present (Miller, chapter VI).
source_locator: R2225: ch. VI and note 13; R2228: vol. 1 of the same compilation, used for the army earlier orders
current_activity: army headquarters and main body assembled on Guadalcanal
notes: Miller, chapter VI: by mid-October 1942 General Hyakutake had assembled a sizable portion of 17th Army, except the main body of the 38th Division, on Guadalcanal, and intended to command the operation in person. The claim date 15 October is mid-month, not a single landing day for the headquarters. Confidence 0.5 (Miller’s mid-October phrase; a day-level landing log for the headquarters was not read). Rabaul remains the earlier rear headquarters (Miller, ch. IV) and is not given a claim in this increment.

location_qualifier: counter-offensive against the Lunga perimeter and Henderson Field
composing_text: The 2nd Division infantry regiments made the inland assault; the 4th, 16th and 29th Infantry are named in Miller, chapter VI, among the units whose combat strength was reduced.
source_locator: R2225: ch. VI (The October Counteroffensive); R2226: the October battles
current_activity: directing the October counter-offensive against the airfield
notes: Miller, chapter VI, and Zimmerman: the Japanese October counter-offensive against the Lunga airfield was fought on 23–26 October 1942. The claim date is 24 October, in the main infantry assaults. Confidence 0.7.

location_qualifier: Guadalcanal, now under 8th Area Army for the Solomons
source_locator: R2228: JACAR C25080231800, 件名 on operations 27 November–2 December (第八方面軍司令官及第十八軍司令官は十一月二十六日総帥を発動し第十七軍司令官は東部ニューギニヤ方面の作戦指揮を第十八軍司令官に移譲しソロモン群島方面の作戦に専任する事となれり)
current_activity: coming under 8th Area Army and specializing in the Solomons
notes: JACAR 17th Army operations record, vol. 1: on 26 November 1942 the 8th Area Army and 18th Army commanders assumed command; 17th Army transferred its eastern New Guinea operations to 18th Army and specialized in the Solomons. Confidence 0.5 (one Japanese official family; the metadata excerpt of that item was read, not every image of the volume). Location remains the army on Guadalcanal; 8th Area Army headquarters at Rabaul has no claim in this increment.

location_qualifier: still on Guadalcanal; exact army headquarters that night was not copied from a page read
source_locator: R2230: C25080236900, order reached HQ the night of 15 January and was delivered to the army commander early on the 16th; R2225: ch. XV (Hyakutake received the order on 15 January)
current_activity: receiving the 8th Area Army order to evacuate Guadalcanal
notes: JACAR vol. 2: 8th Area Army staff officers Imoto and Sato reached 17th Army headquarters on the night of 15 January 1943 with the IGHQ-based withdrawal order and delivered it to the army commander early on the 16th. Miller, chapter XV, says Hyakutake received the order on 15 January. The claim date is 15 January, the night the order reached the headquarters (the two families agree on that arrival). The one-day difference over when the commander himself was briefed is noted, not resolved in a conflict group. Confidence 0.5 (agreement on the order reaching the army, not on a verified headquarters pin; Kokumbona is used as a mid-January west-coast area with 10 km precision because the exact headquarters that night was not copied). IGHQ had decided on 31 December 1942 to abandon the recapture and had ordered 8th Area Army on 4 January (JACAR C25080236800; Miller, ch. XV).

location_qualifier: beginning the withdrawal west from the Kokumbona area toward Cape Esperance
source_locator: R2225: ch. XV (The 17th Army began its withdrawal to Cape Esperance on the night of 22–23 January)
current_activity: beginning the withdrawal to Cape Esperance
notes: Miller, chapter XV: the 17th Army began its withdrawal to Cape Esperance on the night of 22–23 January 1943. The claim date is 23 January, the morning after that night started. Confidence 0.5 (one US official family; a matching calendar sentence was not copied from a JACAR excerpt in this increment).

location_qualifier: last destroyer lift from the Cape Esperance / Kamimbo area
source_locator: R2230: C25080237200 (二月八日迄にブーゲンビル島ユレベンタに上陸); R2225: ch. XV (evacuated on the nights of 1–2, 4–5 and 7–8 February)
current_activity: completing the evacuation from Cape Esperance
notes: JACAR vol. 2: evacuees had landed at Evrenata on Bougainville by 8 February 1943. Miller, chapter XV: the rescuing destroyers evacuated troops on the nights of 1–2, 4–5 and 7–8 February. Confidence 0.7 (Japanese official and US Army official agree that the evacuation was complete with the 7–8 February lift). Miller’s evacuee total (about 13,000, given after the war) and JACAR’s army-only figures (about 9,800 or, in a related catalog excerpt, about 12,000) are not reconciled here.
